pr_title: Ensure dynamicMapping updates are handled in insertion order
pr_body:
The switch to holding dynamic fields in a hashmap effectively randomizes their iteration order. This can be troublesome when building the mapping update required by these updates. When iterating in an unknown order, recursing to the leaf mapper can occur many times `O(n^2)`. However, starting with insertion order, it will occur only `O(n)` times.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/103011
pr_comments: Hi @benwtrent, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

I confirmed this fix by running: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/103015

The runtime is now at or below what it was in 8.10.

I additionally double checked that the flame graphs were similar, and indeed they are.

To clarify to folks digging between all the various issues, this PR didn't fully address the problem. See https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/103011#issuecomment-1874539428. 

The real fix was in 8.11.4, and was a full revert of the originating bugged code.

issue_context.title: Significant ingest performance regression while handling parsing dynamically added objects
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.11+

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

any

### Problem Description

While indexing documents with dynamically added fields, if multiple of those fields are objects are are deeper than 3-5 objects, performance is degraded significantly.

This bug was introduced in: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/90674

### Steps to Reproduce

I built a micro-benchmark to replicate this particular bug. 

But, any dynamic object parsing will cause this.

To mitigate the issue, statically mapped fields for objects is required. 

### Logs (if relevant)

Attached are two JFR files indicating the difference between when the bug was introduce vs. not.
[Archive 2.zip](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/13569248/Archive.2.zip)
comments:
Pinging @elastic/es-search (Team:Search)
I have confirmed this is still not fixed. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/103047 improved parsing by 10x, but its still about 10x slower than before. 

So now, in 8.11.3, instead of 100x slower, parsing is only 10x slower. Digging into the cause to see what other options there are.

I adjusted the benchmark to add some variety to the document "nested ness".

Before this fix:
 - `150584.973 ms/op`

After this fix:
 - `11237.001 ms/op`

So, an improvement of over a magnitude. But, previous to 8.11:
 - `692.411 ms/op`

So, still about a magnitude slower. 

Results with an updated benchmark that dynamically adjusts the depth of docs being created.
[jfr_results.zip](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/13813953/jfr_results.zip)
